findings.summary: A stale guardian progress401 clears a newly authenticated student’s UI session and moves focus to login even though the student remains authenticated.
findings.fix: Capture an authentication generation or requesting user identity before fetch; process401 by signing out only if that generation is still current. Abort or invalidate pending progress requests on role changes. Test an old guardian401 after student login and a current-session401.
findings.evidence: Hold guardian GET /students/:id/progress, log out, log in as student via UI, wait for loaded home and enabled login submit, then return held401. Before: student, focus student-list-open; after: user=null, signed-out, focus login-role-student. /local/me returns200 for the same student both times; no page errors. /tmp/reaudit-312a607/stale401-results.json

passed: Student-name prefixes remain present in concurrent loading, empty, and error status messages; messages stay polite persistent status nodes.
A held successful progress response after roster replacement populated neither the detached disclosure nor its replacement.
Wizard source clearing and nested input/change events produced coherent final source/consent state and no page errors.
Guide bulk expansion exposed its status and matching expanded panel states; refreshed images are outside live regions.
notes: The401 behavior originates in the unchanged generic request helper and is exposed by the newly added asynchronous T5 progress path; it was not introduced by the latest student-name/source-reset fix.
Duplicate display-name progress messages remain ambiguous; the shared identity defect is reported once in aria-specialist.json.
Known baseline sample-assignment loading silence, late-cancel behavior, and stale URL labels were excluded from new findings.
Actual VoiceOver/NVDA was unavailable. Verification uses real browser DOM/focus/AX, disposable local accounts, held mock responses, and no provider calls.

Evidence: /tmp/reaudit-312a607/aria-live-results.json and /tmp/reaudit-312a607/stale401-results.json. Source assertions in committed browser tests do not exercise stale progress401 after role changes.
